# Example: Presentation — Narrated Deck {.unnumbered}

:::: {.callout-warning title="Illustrative example — do not copy"}
This is **one** worked example on the class NHANES dataset, written by a *fictional* group, to show the expected **structure and depth** of a good submission. Your project must use **your own** question, data, audience, and analysis — do not copy this text or these files. This example lives in the public book for learning; graders assess your original work.
::::

Below is the *Cedar Equity Lab* group's `m5-presentation` submission from the worked NHANES example. See the [Presentation brief](../m5-presentation/README.md) for what is required.


---

*File: `ai-use-note.md`*

## AI-use note

AI suggested shorter slide titles and identified jargon in the first draft.
The group checked the 57,137 cohort count, missingness values, three displayed
means, figure labels, and source note against the final report and rendered
slides. We rejected a suggested phrase that implied income predicted BMI.


---

*File: `peer-feedback-received.md`*

## Peer feedback received on the NHANES project

This is inward-facing feedback on our NHANES project. It is separate from the
outward-facing M4 review we wrote about the Northside Active Living project.

- **Source:** River Health Team's review of our M3 report and KT preview.
- **Feedback received:** Say explicitly that the overall difference is small;
  use “Average BMI (kg/m²)” rather than “Mean BMI” in the audience-facing
  dashboard; and keep the unweighted limitation beside the figure.
- **Changes made:** We added “modest/small” to the report and slides, expanded
  the dashboard label and units, and placed the descriptive/unweighted caution
  in the dashboard figure caption and limitation section.
- **Suggestion not adopted:** The reviewers suggested a second dashboard
  control for age range. We kept one income-group control because the current
  audience question is answered without added complexity.

*File: `presentation-checklist.md`*

## Presentation checklist

- [x] Six-slide story fits a seven-minute practice run.
- [x] Audience, question, and KT purpose are visible near the start.
- [x] Data source, adult cohort, and missingness are stated.
- [x] Main figure title, units, source boundary, and limitation are readable.
- [x] Interpretation remains descriptive and non-causal.
- [x] Privacy and stewardship caution is included in the source note.
- [x] Slides render from the project root without local-only files.
- [x] Final slide gives a practical next analytic question.
- [x] Backup notes include source, cohort, and AI-use details.

*File: `source-and-limitations-note.md`*

## Source and limitations note

- **Source:** Prepared classroom snapshot derived from CDC/NCHS National
  Health and Nutrition Examination Survey public-use files;
  `https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/`
- **Inclusion/exclusion:** Ages 20-80 inclusive; grouped results use non-missing
  age, BMI, and income group; cycle figure also requires a non-missing cycle
- **Claim type:** Descriptive and unweighted, not predictive or causal
- **Privacy/stewardship caution:** Show aggregate results only, avoid
  stigmatizing income groups, and do not upload row-level records to AI tools
- **Limitation to say aloud:** The analysis does not use the NHANES survey
  design and is not a national estimate
